name: OSO.L1
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d ∣ n
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n ∧ d ∣ n ∧ d.Coprime (n / d) := by
    -- Extract the conditions from the membership in properUnitaryDivisors
    have h₁ : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := hd
    have h₂ : d ∈ {d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n | d ∣ n ∧ d.Coprime (n / d)} := by
      simpa [properUnitaryDivisors] using h₁
    -- Simplify the membership condition
    have h₃ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n ∧ d ∣ n ∧ d.Coprime (n / d) := by
      simpa using h₂
    exact h₃
  
  have h₂ : d ∣ n := by
    -- Extract the divisibility condition from h₁
    have h₃ : d ∣ n := h₁.2.1
    exact h₃
  
  exact h₂

name: OSO.L2
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
    rw [Finset.mem_Ico]
    <;> omega
  
  have h₂ : 1 ∣ n := by
    exact Nat.one_dvd n
  
  have h₃ : Nat.Coprime 1 (n / 1) := by
    have h₄ : n / 1 = n := by
      simp
    rw [h₄]
    -- We need to show that gcd(1, n) = 1.
    -- Since gcd(a, b) = gcd(a, b - a), we can use the property of gcd.
    -- Here, gcd(1, n) = gcd(1, n - 1) = 1.
    -- However, since 1 is a special case, we can directly use the fact that gcd(1, n) = 1 for any n.
    simp [Nat.coprime_iff_gcd_eq_one, Nat.gcd_comm]
    <;>
    (try omega) <;>
    (try
      {
        cases n with
        | zero => contradiction -- n cannot be zero since hn : 1 < n
        | succ n =>
          simp [Nat.gcd_eq_right_iff_dvd, Nat.dvd_one]
          <;>
          omega
      })
    <;>
    omega
  
  have h₄ : 1 ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := by
    rw [properUnitaryDivisors]
    simp_all [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ico, Nat.div_eq_of_lt]
    <;>
    (try omega) <;>
    (try
      {
        cases n with
        | zero => contradiction -- n cannot be zero since hn : 1 < n
        | succ n =>
          simp_all [Nat.div_eq_of_lt]
          <;>
          omega
      })
    <;>
    (try
      {
        simp_all [Nat.div_eq_of_lt]
        <;>
        omega
      })
    <;>
    (try
      {
        omega
      })
  
  exact h₄

name: OSO.L3
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : properUnitaryDivisors n ⊆ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
    intro d hd
    simp only [properUnitaryDivisors, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_Ico] at hd ⊢
    <;> aesop
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L4
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : properUnitaryDivisors 1 = ∅ := by
    rw [properUnitaryDivisors]
    -- We need to show that the set of proper unitary divisors of 1 is empty.
    -- This is because Finset.Ico 1 1 is empty and the set is defined as a subset of it.
    simp [Finset.Ico_eq_empty_iff, Nat.lt_succ_iff]
    <;> aesop
  
  have h₂ : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors 1, i = 0 := by
    rw [h₁]
    simp [Finset.sum_empty]
    <;> aesop
  
  have h₃ : ¬ (0 = 1 ∧ 0 < 1) := by
    intro h
    have h₄ : 0 = 1 := h.1
    have h₅ : 0 < 1 := h.2
    -- Since 0 ≠ 1, we derive a contradiction.
    norm_num at h₄
    <;> simp_all (config := {decide := true})
    <;> aesop
  
  have h₄ : ¬ IsUnitaryPerfect 1 := by
    intro h
    have h₅ : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors 1, i = 1 ∧ 0 < 1 := h
    have h₆ : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors 1, i = 0 := h₂
    have h₇ : 0 = 1 ∧ 0 < 1 := by
      constructor
      · -- Prove 0 = 1
        linarith
      · -- Prove 0 < 1
        linarith
    exact h₃ h₇
  
  exact h₄

name: OSO.L5
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : n ≠ 1 := by
    by_contra h
    -- Assume n = 1 and derive a contradiction.
    have h₂ : n = 1 := by simpa using h
    have h₃ : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n, i = n := hn.1
    have h₄ : 0 < n := hn.2
    rw [h₂] at h₃
    -- For n = 1, properUnitaryDivisors 1 is empty.
    have h₅ : properUnitaryDivisors 1 = ∅ := by
      rfl
    rw [h₅] at h₃
    -- The sum of the empty set is 0, but n = 1, so 0 ≠ 1.
    norm_num at h₃
    <;> simp_all [Finset.sum_empty]
    <;> aesop
  
  have h₂ : 1 < n := by
    by_contra h
    -- If n ≤ 1, then n = 1 because n > 0.
    have h₃ : n ≤ 1 := by linarith
    have h₄ : n > 0 := hn.2
    have h₅ : n = 1 := by
      omega
    -- This contradicts h₁ : n ≠ 1.
    contradiction
  
  exact h₂

name: OSO.L6
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : Nat.Coprime d (n / d)
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : Nat.Coprime d (n / d) := by
    have h₁ : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := hd
    have h₂ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n ∧ d ∣ n ∧ d.Coprime (n / d) := by
      simpa [properUnitaryDivisors] using h₁
    exact h₂.2.2
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L7
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d < n
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : d < n := by
    have h₂ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
      -- Extract the fact that d is in Finset.Ico 1 n from the membership in properUnitaryDivisors n
      simp only [properUnitaryDivisors, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_singleton] at hd
      -- Simplify the condition to get d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n
      aesop
    -- Use the fact that d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n to get d < n
    have h₃ : d < n := Finset.mem_Ico.mp h₂ |>.2
    exact h₃
  exact h₁

name: OSO.L8
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : Finset.Ico 1 1 = ∅ := by
    apply Finset.Ico_eq_empty_of_le
    <;> norm_num
  
  have h₂ : properUnitaryDivisors 1 = ∅ := by
    rw [show properUnitaryDivisors 1 = {d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 1 | d ∣ 1 ∧ d.Coprime (1 / d)} by rfl]
    rw [h₁]
    <;> simp [Finset.filter_empty]
    <;> aesop
  
  apply h₂

name: OSO.L9
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : properUnitaryDivisors 0 = ∅ := by
    rw [properUnitaryDivisors]
    -- We need to show that the set {d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 0 | d ∣ 0 ∧ d.Coprime (0 / d)} is empty.
    -- Since Finset.Ico 1 0 is empty, the set is automatically empty.
    have h₂ : Finset.Ico 1 0 = ∅ := by
      -- Prove that Finset.Ico 1 0 is empty.
      simp [Finset.Ico_eq_empty_of_le]
    -- Now we can rewrite the set using h₂.
    rw [h₂]
    -- The set {d ∈ ∅ | ...} is empty because there are no elements in ∅.
    simp
  -- The final result follows from h₁.
  exact h₁

name: OSO.L10
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d * (n / d) = n
proof:
:= by
  have h₁ : d ∣ n := by
    have h₂ : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := hd
    have h₃ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n ∧ d ∣ n ∧ Nat.Coprime d (n / d) := by
      simpa [properUnitaryDivisors] using h₂
    exact h₃.2.1
  
  have h₂ : d * (n / d) = n := by
    have h₃ : d ∣ n := h₁
    have h₄ : d * (n / d) = n := by
      apply Nat.mul_div_cancel' h₃
    exact h₄
  
  exact h₂

name: OSO.L11
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : Odd d
proof:
:= by
  have h_dvd_n : d ∣ n := by
    have h₁ : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := hd
    have h₂ : d ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n ∧ d ∣ n ∧ d.Coprime (n / d) := by
      simpa [properUnitaryDivisors] using h₁
    exact h₂.2.1
  
  have h_main : Odd d := by
    have h₁ : d ∣ n := h_dvd_n
    have h₂ : Odd n := hn
    have h₃ : ¬Even n := by
      intro h
      have h₄ : Even n := h
      rw [Nat.even_iff] at h₄
      have h₅ : n % 2 = 0 := by omega
      have h₆ : Odd n := hn
      rw [Nat.odd_iff] at h₆
      omega
    have h₄ : ¬Even d := by
      intro h
      have h₅ : Even d := h
      rw [Nat.even_iff] at h₅
      have h₆ : 2 ∣ d := by omega
      have h₇ : 2 ∣ n := dvd_trans h₆ h₁
      have h₈ : Even n := by
        rw [Nat.even_iff]
        omega
      contradiction
    have h₅ : Odd d := by
      rw [Nat.odd_iff]
      have h₆ : ¬Even d := h₄
      have h₇ : ¬(2 ∣ d) := by
        intro h
        have h₈ : Even d := by
          rw [Nat.even_iff]
          omega
        contradiction
      omega
    exact h₅
  
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L12
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : properUnitaryDivisors p = {1} := by
    apply Finset.ext
    intro d
    simp only [properUnitaryDivisors, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_singleton]
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if d is in properUnitaryDivisors p, then d = 1
      intro h
      have h₁ : 1 ≤ d := by linarith
      have h₂ : d < p := by linarith
      have h₃ : d ∣ p := by tauto
      have h₄ : Nat.Coprime d (p / d) := by tauto
      have h₅ : d = 1 := by
        have h₅₁ : d ∣ p := h₃
        have h₅₂ : d ≤ p := Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.Prime.pos hp) h₅₁
        have h₅₃ : d < p := h₂
        have h₅₄ : d = 1 := by
          by_contra h₅₄
          have h₅₅ : d ≠ 1 := h₅₄
          have h₅₆ : d > 1 := by
            by_contra h₅₆
            have h₅₇ : d ≤ 1 := by linarith
            have h₅₈ : d = 1 := by
              omega
            contradiction
          have h₅₉ : d ∣ p := h₃
          have h₅₁₀ : d = p := by
            have h₅₁₁ : d ∣ p := h₃
            have h₅₁₂ : d ≤ p := Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.Prime.pos hp) h₅₁₁
            have h₅₁₃ : d ≥ 2 := by omega
            have h₅₁₄ : d = p := by
              have h₅₁₅ := Nat.Prime.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd hp d h₅₁₁
              omega
            exact h₅₁₄
          have h₅₁₁ : d < p := h₂
          omega
        exact h₅₄
      simp_all
    · -- Prove the reverse direction: if d = 1, then d is in properUnitaryDivisors p
      intro h
      have h₁ : d = 1 := by simp_all
      rw [h₁]
      have h₂ : 1 < p := Nat.Prime.one_lt hp
      have h₃ : 1 ∣ p := by
        exact Nat.one_dvd p
      have h₄ : Nat.Coprime 1 (p / 1) := by
        simp [Nat.coprime_one_left]
      have h₅ : 1 < p := Nat.Prime.one_lt hp
      constructor
      · -- Prove 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 1 p
        constructor <;> omega
      · -- Prove 1 ∣ p ∧ Nat.Coprime 1 (p / 1)
        constructor <;> simp_all [Nat.coprime_one_left]
        <;> omega
  
  have h_sum : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors p, i = 1 := by
    rw [h_main]
    simp [Finset.sum_singleton]
    <;>
    aesop
  
  have h_false : ¬ IsUnitaryPerfect p := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : ∑ i ∈ properUnitaryDivisors p, i = p := h.1
    have h₂ : 0 < p := h.2
    rw [h_sum] at h₁
    have h₃ : p = 1 := by linarith
    have h₄ : p.Prime := hp
    have h₅ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le h₄
    linarith
  
  exact h_false

name: OSO.L13
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : n ∉ properUnitaryDivisors n := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
      have h₂ : n ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := h
      have h₃ : n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
        -- Prove that n is in the Finset.Ico 1 n using the definition of properUnitaryDivisors
        have h₄ : n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
          -- Use the fact that n is in properUnitaryDivisors n to get the required condition
          have h₅ : n ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n := h₂
          have h₆ : n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
            -- Use the definition of properUnitaryDivisors to get the required condition
            simp [properUnitaryDivisors, Finset.mem_Ico] at h₅ ⊢
            <;> aesop
          exact h₆
        exact h₄
      exact h₃
    -- Derive a contradiction from the fact that n is in Finset.Ico 1 n
    have h₂ : n ∉ Finset.Ico 1 n := by
      -- Prove that n is not in Finset.Ico 1 n
      simp [Finset.mem_Ico]
      <;> omega
    exact h₂ h₁
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L14
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n := by
    -- Use the lemma `Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd` to find a prime `p` that divides `n`.
    have h₁ : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n := by
      -- Apply the lemma `Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd` which states that for any `n > 1`, there exists a prime `p` such that `p ∣ n`.
      apply Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd
      <;> omega
    -- The result follows directly from the lemma.
    exact h₁
  -- The final result is already obtained in `h_main`.
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L15
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hd : p ∣ n) : 0 < n.factorization p
proof:
:= by
  have h_main : 0 < n.factorization p := by
    have h₁ : p ∣ n := hd
    have h₂ : p.Prime := hp
    have h₃ : n.factorization p > 0 := by
      -- Use the fact that if a prime divides a number, its factorization is positive
      have h₄ : p ∣ n := h₁
      have h₅ : n.factorization p > 0 := by
        -- Use the property of prime factorization
        have h₆ : p.Prime := h₂
        have h₇ : p ∣ n := h₄
        have h₈ : n.factorization p > 0 := by
          -- Use the fact that if a prime divides a number, its factorization is positive
          apply Nat.pos_of_ne_zero
          intro h
          have h₉ := Nat.Prime.ne_zero h₆
          have h₁₀ := Nat.Prime.ne_zero h₆
          simp_all [Nat.factorization_eq_zero_iff]
          <;> aesop
        exact h₈
      exact h₅
    exact h₃
  exact h_main

name: OSO.L16
statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) : (1 : ℕ) ≠ p ^ k
proof:
:= by
  have h_p_ge_two : 2 ≤ p := by
    have h := hp.two_le
    exact h
  
  have h_k_ge_one : 1 ≤ k := by
    omega
  
  have h_one_lt_pow : 1 < p ^ k := by
    have h₁ : 1 < p := by
      linarith [h_p_ge_two]
    have h₂ : 1 < p ^ k := by
      apply Nat.one_lt_pow (by omega)
      <;> omega
    exact h₂
  
  have h_main : (1 : ℕ) ≠ p ^ k := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : 1 < p ^ k := h_one_lt_pow
    linarith
  
  exact h_main
